title: Forensics SIEM archive playbook for private deployments
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the recommended end-to-end SIEM and evidence-archive workflow for Redwood Private deployments. It emphasizes forensic readiness: RBAC controls for evidence access, a compact audit-log schema for correlation, secure SIEM export patterns, and automated bundling with chain-of-custody metadata. Intended audience: SRE, infra security, solutions engineering, and compliance reviewers working on VPC/on-prem deployments.

Objectives:
- Ensure investigators can assemble timelines across VPC flow, firewall, and mTLS events quickly.
- Preserve immutable evidence with verifiable hashes and signatures.
- Limit access by RBAC v2 roles and produce immutable access logs.
- Provide repeatable collector and SIEM ingest patterns for common SIEM vendors.

Minimal audit-log schema (canonical fields):
- timestamp: UTC ISO8601
- event_id: uuid4
- event_type: vpc_flow | firewall_allow | firewall_deny | mtls_handshake | mtls_failure | host_syslog | process_start | net_conn | auth_attempt | config_change
- src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port
- src_identity, dst_identity (string tokens for the principal)
- protocol: tcp|udp|icmp|other
- action: allow|deny|reset|observe|start|stop|fail|success
- bytes_sent, bytes_recv (optional)
- session_id: correlation token
- cert_fingerprint: sha256 or empty
- auth_mechanism: mTLS|oauth|apikey|none
- user_agent (optional)
- log_source: host-id | vpc-flow-collector | firewall-id
- ingestion_timestamp: when collector forwarded the event
- provenance: brief collection descriptor
- raw_payload: optional truncated blob (max 8k)

Practical notes:
- Keep raw_payload small to control SIEM costs. Use session_id and event_id for stitching instead of embedding large payloads.
- Use NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) for transport. Compress payloads in small chunks (gzip) and rely on event_id dedupe in the SIEM.

RBAC v2 for forensic assets (recommended roles/policies):
- incident_first_responder: create bundles, view redacted logs, limited time-limited elevated sessions.
- incident_lead: full access to evidence bundles and exports.
- compliance_reviewer: read-only to archived bundles with redaction enforced.
- infra_admin: manage collectors and configs, no evidence access by default.
- platops_readonly: live dashboards only.

Enforcement integration points:
- Collector API: validate RBAC token on bundle creation and retrieval.
- Archive storage: bucket/object ACLs mapped to RBAC roles; use object-lock for retention.
- SIEM gating: tokenized queries so SIEM can honor Redwood roles where the SIEM supports it.
- Immutable access log: every retrieval must append to a write-only access ledger.

Collector topologies and transport patterns:
- Push collector (recommended if outbound allowed): local agent tails logs and pushes via mTLS to a collector cluster that forwards to SIEM.
- Pull collector (air-gapped): central collector pulls data over a bastion using approved protocols; ensure strong logging of pull actions.
- Transport: TLS1.2+ with mutual auth; rotate client certs automatically.
- Buffering: support disk-backed queues; alert when queue exceeds threshold.

SIEM ingest guidance by vendor:
- Elastic: Filebeat -> Logstash -> Elasticsearch. Index by event_type with ILM hot->warm->cold. Retention example: 90d hot, 365d cold for security events. Use pipeline processors to trim raw_payload.
- Splunk: Heavy forwarder -> Indexer. Use event_id for dedupe. Use summary indexing for VPC flow volumes.

Evidence bundle lifecycle and manifest format:
- Triggering: manual (investigator) or auto-rule-based (e.g., spike in mtls failures + unusual egress).
- Contents: targeted host pcaps, VPC flow slices, firewall logs, collector metadata, config snapshots, certs, and SIEM search query used to assemble data.
- Organization: /bundle-{id}/hosts/, /bundle-{id}/vpc/, /bundle-{id}/firewall/, /bundle-{id}/manifests/
- manifest.json fields (flat): bundle_id, created_by, created_at, ticket_id, items_list (comma-separated paths), total_size, bundle_sha256, signature_base64
- Storage: encrypted object in customer archive with object-lock or on-prem WORM vault.
- Verification: sha256 per file and overall bundle hash recorded in append-only ledger.

Chain-of-custody practices:
- Sign manifest with private key and store public key fingerprint in ledger.
- Record who initiated bundle, who accessed it, and why (ticket id).
- Expire access grants automatically and require reauthorization for export.

Firewall and VPC hardened patterns (short checklist):
- Default deny; explicit allow with minimal port/CIDR.
- Egress through NGFW/egress proxy appliance.
- Tag rules with intent and sequencing numbers.
- Enable VPC flow logs at subnet/ENI level; sample full flows when budget allows.
- Log mTLS handshake outcomes and cert fingerprints at ingress and internal gateways.

Incident runbook (quick steps):
1) Triage: assemble timeline via event_id/session_id correlation across SIEM searches.
2) Contain: apply ephemeral deny rules scoped to session or host.
3) Evidence: create bundle covering +/- 15 minutes around suspected activity.
4) Notify: attach bundle path and manifest to incident ticket; notify legal/compliance if required.
5) Remediate: rotate certs/keys and document in audit stream.

Short commands for on-host collection (examples):
- tcpdump for short capture: sudo timeout 60 tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/forensic-$(date -u +%s).pcap '(tcp or udp) and host 10.2.3.4'
- iptables snapshot: sudo iptables-save > /tmp/iptables-$(date -u +%s).conf
- process listing: ps auxf > /tmp/ps-$(date -u +%s).txt
- hashing: sha256sum /tmp/forensic-*.pcap > /tmp/forensic.hashes

Starter detection rules and dashboards:
- Repeated mtls_handshake failures across client fleet.
- Large egress flows to unknown IPs outside allow-list.
- Sudden spike in unique dst_ports from single internal src_ip.
- Collectors lagging behind or failing cert rotation.

Appendix: simplified ASCII flow

Customer VPC: [app subnet] -> [ingress gateway (mTLS)] -> [internal services] -> [egress proxy/NGFW] -> Internet
                 |
                 v
            Collectors (mTLS) -> SIEM -> Archive (WORM)

Open items and engineering tasks:
- Implement reversible redaction at collector side to allow compliance reviewers filtered views.
- Add deterministic dedupe support for sampled flow events in SIEM.
- Validate S3 object-lock replication and legal hold processes for multi-region retention.

References:
- Internal: Private Deploy Audit Schema (confluence link above).
- External: NIST 800-92, OWASP Logging Guide.

Owner and contact: Ava Mitchell, #eng-private-deployments on Slack.
